Implement the following requested change in the repository.

When SQLFluff lint folder, the exit code depends on the last file
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

When I upgraded to SQLFluff 3.0.0, I found that the `sqlfluff lint .` command executed in CI did not fail, even though there were files that found issues.

After some simple debugging, I found that when linting a folder, the exit code depends on the last file: If the last file found the issue, the command result is `FAIL`; If not issue is found in the last file, the command result is `SUCCESS`.

### Expected Behaviour

When running the `sqlfluff lint .` command, if any issues are found with the file, exit code return 1 or 2. 

Just like it says in the [document](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/85c85bf0dedb9608e300e1214fa0e3a0b7228f1d/docs/source/production.rst?plain=1#L66-L81).

```
The `exit code`_ provided by SQLFluff when run as a command line utility is
designed to assist usefulness in deployment pipelines. If no violations
are found then the `exit code`_ will be 0. If violations are found then
a non-zero code will be returned which can be interrogated to find out
more.

- An error code of ``0`` means *operation success*, *no issues found*.
- An error code of ``1`` means *operation success*, *issues found*. For
  example this might mean that a linting issue was found, or that one file
  could not be parsed.
- An error code of ``2`` means an error occurred and the operation could
  not be completed. For example a configuration issue or an internal error
  within SQLFluff.
```

### Observed Behaviour

When running the `sqlfluff lint .` command, the exit code depends on the last file:

* When the last file not issues found, exit code is 0.
* When the last file issues found, exit code is 1.

> PS: At the same time, I tested it in 2.3.5 and did not find this issue.

### How to reproduce

SQLFluff is executed in alphabetical order in the directory, so creating two files to make one of them fail can verify this conclusion.

## It is not the last file that failed, the result is `SUCCESS`

1. Create an empty directory

```bash
mkdir sqlfluff-playgrand
```

2. Create the two sql files: `1.sql`, `2.sql`. `1.sql` will fail and `2.sql` will pass.

The content of `1.sql` is as follows:
```sql
select
    column
from table
```

The content of `2.sql` is as follows:
```sql
select column
from table
```

3. running the `sqlfluff lint . --dialect ansi` in the directory, will return `SUCCESS` results

```bash
sqlfluff lint . --dialect ansi
== [path/test-playgrand/1.sql] FAIL
L:   1 | P:   1 | LT09 | Select targets should be on a new line unless there is
                       | only one select target.
                       | [layout.select_targets]
All Finished 📜 🎉! 
```
